actions: Audited public Saga and transactional-outbox guidance for multi-participant eventual consistency, stale concurrency and idempotency separation.
Executed a 288-scenario two-sink finite model with asynchronous authority transitions, ambiguous response, expiring dedupe, verifier outage and exact staged-contract reuse.

Compared scalar latest-epoch terminality, historical/vector labels without sink proof, per-sink atomic receipts with ephemeral versus durable effect identities, exact staged reuse and serial fail-closed behavior.
Persisted executable model, result JSON and role-local checkpoint.

generic_residual_capability_boundary.minimum_generic_effect: Each authoritative effect sink must provide an atomic current-authority check (or equivalent server invariant) at effect application and enough durable effect identity/status to reconcile ambiguous application. CLEAN can construct claims, vectors, immutable stages and parent completeness certificates, but cannot install or globally validate those protected sink invariants.

termination.reason: Multi-sink vector leaf completed and refined parent terminality into per-effect apply-time authority receipts plus durable effect identity.

exact_continuation: Next non-conflicting Phase-1 leaf: certificate revocation semantics and irreversible-vs-revocable effects. Introduce effect contracts IRREVERSIBLE_ONCE_AUTHORIZED / REVOCABLE_UNTIL_PARENT_TERMINAL / COMPENSATABLE, then advance a sink or parent epoch after a valid apply-time receipt but before parent terminality. Compare historical apply-time certificate, current-epoch-only certificate, explicit revocation tombstone, compensation receipt, and fail-closed. Test whether later epoch does not invalidate old receipt is safe only for irreversible authorization semantics, and derive a terminality predicate that carries effect revocability/compensation state rather than assuming one rule for all sinks. Include ambiguous compensation response and durable effect identity.
